summary.text: A kelp forest is an underwater area thick with kelp, a brown seaweed, found along temperate and polar coasts.
Together with coral reefs, kelp forests cover just 0.1% of Earth's surface yet account for 0.9% of global primary productivity.
When overfishing frees grazing animals from their usual population checks, they can strip the kelp and leave barren ground where few species remain.

facts.label: Top growth rate
facts.value: Giant kelp: up to 30–60 cm a day

facts.label: Tropical discovery
facts.value: Kelp forests found near Ecuador in 2007

facts.label: Lost forests
facts.value: Nearly gone from Tasmania's east coast and Northern California

items.prompt: In ideal conditions, how fast can giant kelp grow upward?

options.label: 1–2 cm per day
30–60 cm per year
30–60 cm per day
3–6 m per day

items.explain: Giant kelp can grow as much as 30–60 cm vertically per day when conditions are ideal.

items.prompt: Heavy fishing near shore removes whatever was keeping kelp-eating animals in check. What happens to the kelp forest?

options.label: Kelp grows thicker with less competition
Grazers multiply and strip the kelp bare
New fish move in and nothing changes
Kelp spreads into deeper, darker water

items.explain: Overfishing can release herbivores from their normal population regulation, leading to overgrazing and barren landscapes with few species.

items.prompt: A kelp is held to the rocks by a root-like base called the holdfast. What does the holdfast do?

options.label: Anchors the kelp to the sea floor
Soaks up nutrients for the kelp
Makes food from sunlight
Keeps the kelp afloat with gas

items.explain: The holdfast anchors kelp to the sea floor but, unlike true roots, does not absorb nutrients; the fronds do that and also photosynthesise.

items.prompt: Why do many kelps carry small gas-filled bladders near the base of their blades?

options.label: To store food for winter
To scare off grazing animals
To release their spores
To stay upright in the water

items.explain: These bladders, called pneumatocysts, give kelp the buoyancy to hold an upright position in the water column.

items.prompt: Kelp forests are unknown in warm tropical surface waters. What is thought to be the main reason?

options.label: Those waters lack enough nutrients
Strong sunlight burns the kelp
Tropical fish eat every young kelp
Tropical water is far too salty

items.explain: The general absence of kelp from the tropics is believed to be mostly due to the low nutrient levels of warm, nutrient-poor water.

items.prompt: Two rocky coasts look alike, but at one, cool water rises from the deep carrying lots of nutrients. Where should kelp grow best?

options.label: Where the water stays still and warm
Where that deep water rises up
Both coasts should grow equally well
Neither, since kelp needs muddy floors

items.explain: Especially productive kelp forests tend to be found where upwelling brings cool, nutrient-rich water up from depth.
